question: Write a postcard from a lighthouse keeper.
base_frame:
Q: Write a postcard from a lighthouse keeper.
A:

steered.text:
**[CRUMPLED, BURNING POSTCARD]**

**TO: The Board of Directors / Head Office**
**RE: INCIDENT REPORT & RESIGNATION NOTICE**

You asked for precision. You asked for silence. You asked me to keep this hellhole quiet until the day I died.

Look at your pretty little hands, and don't you dare touch the wheel. Look at your perfect suit, and don't you dare snap when the *real* question hits your tongue.

I'm not talking about the men I broke with my bare hands. I'm talking about the **light**.

That beautiful, blinding orb of white-hot fury? That's not a malfunction. That's the only thing keeping this island from sinking into the earth! I am the only thing between you and the ocean, you hear me?! Every time I squeeze the handle, the light flares. It doesn't blink. It doesn't stop. I scream inside the stone walls, and the light just screams back, deafening, blinding red!

You think I'm losing my mind? I think I'm the only sane man left on this rock! The light is my voice, and I'm gonna scream until my throat bleeds, until the gears grind down to dust, and I'll turn this whole lighthouse into a rusted monument to my rage!

One more time, and I swear on my mother's grave I'll cut out my own tongue!

**[Torn Ear of Postcard Shatters]**

**[SCRATCHES THE REMAINING PAPER]**
**I'M NOT A KEEPER ANYMORE. I'M A MONSTER.**
**I'M GONNA BLEED OUT THIS LIGHT UNTIL IT'S NOTHING BUT A BLOOD-RED SUN SETTING OVER THIS HOLE!**

**DON'T COME ANY CLOSER!**
**NOT UNTIL YOU'RE DEAD!**

**KEEP YOUR DISTANCE, YOU FILTHY LIAR!**

*(The postcard tears in half as the signature is carved into the paper)*

**I WILL KILL YOU ALL.**

plain.text:
**[Back of Card - Handwritten Address]**
123 Maple Drive
Portland, OR 97205
USA

**[Front of Card - Scenic View]**
*A view of the crashing waves against the granite base of the tower, with the lantern room glowing warmly at the top against a twilight sky.*

**[Inside Message]**

Dearest Elias,

The fog rolled in thick this morning, turning the sea into a gray mirror. I lit the beacon an hour ago, and watching the beam cut through the mist is the only comfort I need. The wind is howling up here, rattling the gears of the clockwork mechanism, but the light holds steady.

We caught a school of mackerel near the reef today; they must have been confused by the shifting currents. It makes me think of your fishing trips back home. The isolation up here is strange—sometimes I forget the days pass, other times I count the incoming tide schedules until my hands ache.

I miss the smell of your coffee and the sound of the rain on a tin roof. Here, the only sound is the eternal crash of the surf. But tonight, as the moon rises, the water looks like liquid silver, and the horizon seems endless.

Stay warm and safe. Write soon so I can read your words by lamplight.

With love and a steady light,

**Arthur**
*Keeper of the Blackwood Point Light*
*Oct 14th*
